BiblicalUsage: This word means abhorrence, the thing people turn from in disgust. Daniel sees the wicked rising to shame and everlasting contempt, and Isaiah sees the undying worm and unquenched fire that make the rebels an abhorring to all flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that everlasting contempt is the sober end of refusing God; it is not a word I use lightly, but Scripture uses it, and it tells me how seriously God takes a life that turns from Him for good.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
